newsitem.title: USA: Dlr/mark higher at the US open, dlr/yen struggles.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/mark higher at the US open, dlr/yen struggles.

text.p: Dollar/mark rallied at the start of the U.S. session on Thursday while dollar/yen struggled to hold above a key support level, traders and analysts said.

"The dollar is generally firm against the D-mark and the Swiss franc, and slightly lower versus the Japanese yen and the British pound," said senior currency analyst Marc Chandler at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
At the open, the dollar was quoted at 1.7260/70 marks versus 1.7235/45 at the close on Wednesday, and at 113.50/60 yen versus 113.87/97.
The yen continued to draw some support from Japan's stronger-than-expected tankan report on business conditions while sterling was propped up by prospects of higher U.K. interest rates.

"Dollar/mark is testing the upper end of the current range but has no momentum to speak of," said Chandler, who expected dollar/mark to run out of steam below 1.7320/25, the high on Friday and Monday. "The 1.7320-mark level is the most you can hope for today."
Also pressuring the mark was comments by Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen.
Jochimsen told reporters in Frankfurt "I don't rule out a further interest rate cut but I don't see it."
Jochimsen also said he would support a single European currency if "the political and economic preconditions are right. They are not at the present."
Separately, and as expected, the Bundesbank left Germany's 2.50-percent discount rate, 4.50-percent Lombard rate and 3.0-percent repo rate unchanged at its regular meeting.
"There was no surprise there. It did not help dollar/mark, but it did not hurt either," one trader said. "It's the yen that's the leader again today."
Chandler agreed the yen continued to display strength, particularly versus the mark -- which helps dollar/mark but caps dollar/yen.
"People are selling mark/yen," said Chandler, who commented on that cross's retreat below 66.00.
Technical analysts said mark/yen may lose strong support at 65.50 before bottoming out around 65.25, the recent low set on June 17.
"Dollar/yen should hold below 114.00/20," Chandler predicted. "Japanese exporters are selling the dollar and there is some talk of Asian central banks selling as well."
But Chandler also expected the dollar/yen's downside to be capped at 113.00, a level where "Japanese public funds and institutional funds are buying."

Meanwhile, the Bank of Canada raised the key Bank Rate by 25 basis points to 3.50 percent, effectively raising the overnight lending rate's target range to 3.0-to-3.50 percent from 2.75-to-3.25 percent.

Market watchers said the move was not entirely unexpected because the Bank of Canada's recent intervention pattern indicated concern over an overly stimulative monetary conditions brought about by a weak Canadian dollar.

The Canadian dollar jumped nearly two U.S. cents on the news. The U.S. dollar had been quoted at C$1.3954/59 at the open versus C$1.3935.45 at the close on Wednesday, and set a morning session's low at C$1.3765.
Both U.S. bonds and stocks opened lower following news of a 14,000 drop in jobless claims for the week ended June 21 to 332,000 -- data consistent with strong U.S. job market.
Also at the open, the dollar was quoted at 1.4380/90 Swiss francs, just off 1.4365/75 at the close on Wednesday.
Cable opened at $1.6663/70 versus $1.6630/40 and the Australian dollar was quoted at $.07500, virtually unchanged.
((-- Isabelle Clary, 212-859-1666))
